trial_court: Principal Judge, Family Court, Chikkamagaluru, M.C.No.9/2013 and M.C.No.17/2013
case_name: M Sharath vs A K Krithika
facts_of_case: The parties are M Sharath and A K Krithika, who were married under the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. The husband filed a petition for divorce under Section 13(1) (i) (ia) (ib) of the Hindu Marriage Act, which was dismissed by the trial court. The wife also filed a petition seeking a decree of restitution of conjugal rights, which was allowed by the trial court.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party seeking divorce to prove that the other party has caused mental cruelty without any valid reason.
legal_principles.held: It is averred that first respondent/wife has caused mental cruelty to the appellant/husband without any valid reason.

legal_principles.principle: A party seeking divorce must prove that the other party has deserted them without any valid reason.
legal_principles.held: It is pleaded that even though appellant/husband and first respondent/wife lived together separately for more than 8 years, there is no cohabitation between them and without any reason she left the matrimonial home by deserting the appellant/husband and started living separately since April 2002.

outcome.final_order: The appeals are allowed and the judgment and decree passed by the trial court are set aside. The parties are directed to maintain the status quo until further orders.

use_for_drafting: advising on Hindu Marriage Act provisions
